parts.lead:
Consumer 360° camera from Insta360 with two 1-inch sensors behind back-to-back fisheye lenses of about 200° each and a built-in IMU at 1 kHz. It is the camera of the Hilti-Trimble SLAM Challenge 2026 dataset. Each lens is solved with the IMU from the organisers' own calibration recording, with the rolling-shutter readout estimated. The first tab puts the two solves together as one rig.

360° cameraRolling shutter2 × 200° fisheye1 kHz IMUCC BY-NC-SA data

parts.limits:
• The tab with both lenses is put together from two solves, not one joint solve: each lens is placed in the IMU frame by its own recording. Its IMU values and its calibration-process view are those of the front-lens recording.
  • So the distance between the lenses, about 26 mm, comes from two camera-to-IMU results, not from a direct solve of the pair. The organisers' Kalibr calibration gives about 40 mm, and the difference isn't explained yet. The lenses face opposite ways and rarely see the board together.
  • The organisers publish a Kalibr calibration (EUCM model, IMU intrinsics fixed). It isn't an independent reference: it comes from the same recordings.
  • The board reaches about 95° from the lens axis, so the outermost part of each 200° image is extrapolated.
  • The images are JPEG-compressed, which can shift detected corners slightly.
parts.run: • Each lens alone with the IMU, then both placed in the one IMU frame. Camera intrinsics (Kannala–Brandt kb4) start from a single-camera solve of the camera-pair recording and stay free; rolling-shutter readout, camera time offset, IMU scale and misalignment and the gyro-to-accel offset t_ga estimated. IMU noise measured on the camera-pair recording, where the camera stands still, and widened about 2.8×. Solved 2026-11-12.
